title: Ask Stovepipe Breaker — Digest + Microprobes
content:
TL;DR: Pulling together a short, pragmatic set of microprobes to break down recurring customer stovepipes — i.e., where a single failure mode (latency spikes, cache invalidation, model fallbacks) produces a wave of distinct helpdesk asks. Goal: translate high-volume, noisy signals into small experiments that engineering can run inside a sprint (2–5 days) and CS can validate with a customer within the same week.

Context and pattern observed:
- Over the last 8 weeks we saw ~62 support threads where customers reported 'sudden latency increases' tied to long-range chat sessions. Many threads conflate: prompt length, KV-cache misses, autoscaler cold starts, and occasional routing to quantized variants.
- Common symptom bundle: sudden token-latency jitter > 300ms at the 2k+ token mark, throughput drop for dedicated pools, and elevated error rates when model rollouts happen.
- Root-cause hypotheses (high level):
  * KV-cache eviction heuristics are not aligned with customer session shapes (long-chat customers losing prefix cached state).
  * Autoscaler warm-up plus initial kernel selection penalty when sequence lengths exceed typical distribution.
  * Routing policies causing fallbacks to quantized variants without transparent signal in logs.

Primary customer asks (distilled):
1) Reduce mid-session latency spikes for long chats (customers: two enterprise PLG apps and one contact-center).
2) Better signal in console and API responses when fallback/variant swap occurs.
3) Easier way to pin or prefer non-quantized variants for latency-sensitive routes.
4) Clear guidance + guardrails for prefix caching config and eviction settings.

Microprobes (small experiments to surface which hypothesis is dominant):
A. Tiny KV-cache thermostat (2d spike):
   - Implement an experiment toggling eviction aggressiveness for one dedicated pool (internal flag: kv.eviction_bias=low).
   - Measure: per-token latency distribution for sessions > 1k tokens, cache-hit ratio, and number of rehydrations.
   - Customer validation: run with 2 enterprise customers for 48h.
B. Warm-start kernel perf sampling (3d):
   - Add sampling hook to record kernel-selection time and first-token latency for long sequences; store in short-term metrics (7d retention).
   - Measure correlation of kernel-selection delay vs latency spike events.
C. Fallback transparency shim (2d + doc):
   - Add a soft-marker in response metadata when routing results in variant swap (e.g., x-rw-variant-swap: quantized-1).
   - Add console alert and an audit row in the request trace so CS can point to exact event.
D. Pin-preference toggle (1d UI + backend flag):
   - Quick UI toggle per-API-key to prefer 'non-quantized' variants; backend honors preference when capacity available. Log fallback reason if preference cannot be honored.

Expected impact and rough cost: (very high-level)
- A/B of A should reduce the 95th percentile mid-session latency for long chats if eviction is a major contributor. Work: small (changes in cache heuristic + rollout).
- B gives us observability; low engineering cost but high value to triage.
- C is low-risk; increases CS troubleshooting speed and reduces misdiagnosed model regressions.
- D is product-facing, small UI surface but requires policy to avoid abuse; useful as a stopgap for enterprise customers.

Customer validation plan:
- Recruit 2–3 customers from existing incident threads (offer controlled test, credits for participation).
- CS to run short interviews pre/post-probe (10–15 min) to capture perceived latency and confidence.
- Use tracing + token-level telemetry to produce before/after delta.

Open questions / risks:
- Will toggling eviction aggressiveness negatively affect other workloads (e.g., short bursty generation)? Need guardrail and canary.
- Pin-preference toggle could concentrate load on non-quantized backends increasing cost — need quotas and soft-fallback warnings.
- Data retention and privacy: kernel-sampling logs include sequence length and timing; ensure we strip user text and follow retention rules.

Operational checklist for running probes quickly:
- SRE: create a dedicated canary pool, add metrics (cache hit ratio, first-token latency, kernel-selection time).
- Serving runtime: add a short-lived feature flag for kv.eviction_bias and variant-transparency header.
- Product/Console: add an ephemeral UI toggle for pinned preference scoped to seat or API key.
- CS: identify customers, draft outreach message, and create a short consent checklist.

Draft outreach message (CS):
- Subject: quick performance test: reduce chat latency spikes
- Body (short): "Hi — we saw intermittent latency spikes in some long chat sessions associated with your workspace. We're running a quick 48h experiment that tweaks our cache behavior and would love to run it on your account. We only need your opt-in; no SDK changes required. We'll share a short before/after with action items. Interested?"

Next steps (owner + timeframe):
- Claire N: finalize microprobe spec and sync with SRE (by 2026-04-12).
- Miguel A: add kernel sampling hooks and metric dashboards (by 2026-04-16).
- Aisha P: draft customer outreach and prepare consent flow (by 2026-04-13).
- Jon P: scope console toggle + backend flag (by 2026-04-20).

Notes to self / conversation fragments: 
- "If eviction is the culprit, we should consider a session-weighted caching mode — not just time-based or LRU." — Miguel
- "Transparency header might be enough for customers to triage without big UX work." — Aisha

References & quick links: 
- Incident thread sampler: #cs-incident-1428 (slack)
- Confluence draft: /display/CS/ask-stovepipe-breaker (linked_artifacts above)
- Related engineering spike: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-ops/issues/216

Appendix: snapshot telemetry queries (for eng) — quick SQL-like pseudocode:
- Sessions with token_count > 1000 and avg_token_latency > 0.2ms: SELECT session_id, token_count, percentiles(token_latency) ...
- Cache-hit ratio by pool: SELECT pool_id, sum(cache_hits)/sum(cache_lookups) ...

—— end of digest ——
